title: Passive Voice in the Past and Present
lede: Form and use past and present passive verbs, promote the affected noun to نائب الفاعل and choose passive voice for a clear communicative reason.
nav: The Subjunctive after أَنْ، لَنْ، كَيْ and حَتَّى

items.prompt: Choose the passive past “The letter was written”.
items.feedback: Form I passive past uses the فُعِلَ vowel pattern.

items.prompt: Choose the passive present “The letter is written”.

items.feedback: The passive focuses on the rule, not the unnamed agent.

items.prompt: In a passive sentence, the former object…
options: becomes the grammatical نائب الفاعل and is nominative
items.feedback: The affected noun takes the subject-like grammatical role.

items.prompt: Choose the passive present of فَتَحَ.

options: To foreground the action/result when the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
items.feedback: Passive is a meaning choice, not decoration.
Past passive and non-human plural feminine singular agreement.
Passive derived form and non-human plural agreement.
Non-human plural takes feminine singular agreement.

options: سَرَقَ الشَّخْصُ الْهَاتِفَ without knowing person

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَسْتَعْمِلُ الْمَبْنِيَّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ؟
Passive voice foregrounds what happened or what is done when the agent is unknown, obvious or less important.
Recognise core Form I past and present passive patterns.
Transform active sentences and apply gender/non-human plural agreement.
Use derived passive forms and explain information focus and case role.
[callout] Communication target: Write a clear notice, report or process using passive forms purposefully.
Distinguish active and passive vowels and roles.
Change the internal vowels and make the affected noun the grammatical focus.

TABLE: Active past | Passive past | Meaning shift // كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الرِّسَالَةَ. | كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ. | The letter/result is foregrounded. // فَتَحَ الْمُوَظَّفُ الْبَابَ. | فُتِحَ الْبَابُ. | The agent is omitted. // كَسَرَ الْوَلَدُ الزُّجَاجَ. | كُسِرَ الزُّجَاجُ. | The affected item becomes نائب الفاعل. // أَعْلَنَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ النَّتِيجَةَ. | أُعْلِنَتِ النَّتِيجَةُ. | Derived forms have their own passive vowel pattern.
[callout] Form I pattern: Active فَعَلَ becomes passive فُعِلَ : كَتَبَ ← كُتِبَ، فَتَحَ ← فُتِحَ .
The passive present is common in notices, processes, formal reports and general statements.

TABLE: Active present | Passive present | Use // يَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبُ الرِّسَالَةَ. | تُكْتَبُ الرِّسَالَةُ. | process/general practice // يَفْتَحُ الْمُوَظَّفُ الْبَابَ. | يُفْتَحُ الْبَابُ. | what happens to the door // يَمْنَعُ الْقَانُونُ التَّدْخِينَ. | يُمْنَعُ التَّدْخِينُ. | rule/sign // يَسْتَعْمِلُ النَّاسُ التِّقْنِيَّةَ. | تُسْتَعْمَلُ التِّقْنِيَّةُ. | formal description
[callout] Form I pattern: Active يَفْعَلُ becomes passive يُفْعَلُ . The subject agreement prefix still matches the affected noun: تُكْتَبُ الرِّسَالَةُ .
The passive changes information focus: action and result move forward; agent moves out.
The speaker does not know who stole it.
The institution is obvious or not important.
[callout/warning] Do not use passive to hide a relevant agent. If who performed the action matters, the active sentence may be clearer.
A reliable transformation protects verb pattern, agreement and case role.

TABLE: Active sentence | Transformation step | Passive result // كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ الرِّسَالَةَ. | 1 change verb vowels; 2 remove agent; 3 raise object | كُتِبَتِ الرِّسَالَةُ. // يَفْتَحُ الْحَارِسُ الْبَابَ. | 1 يُفْعَلُ; 2 remove agent; 3 match الباب | يُفْتَحُ الْبَابُ. // تَسْتَعْمِلُ الشَّرِكَةُ الآلَةَ. | Use derived-form passive stem and feminine agreement | تُسْتَعْمَلُ الآلَةُ. // أَعْلَنَ الْمُدِيرُ النَّتَائِجَ. | Passive past + non-human plural agreement | أُعْلِنَتِ النَّتَائِجُ.
[callout] Case awareness: The former object is no longer accusative. As نَائِبُ الْفَاعِلِ , it is nominative in fully marked Arabic.
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
Passive past needs internal vowel change.
The passive verb agrees with the feminine affected noun.
Choose passive forms with accurate agreement.
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
Read notices and reports; underline passive verbs and identify the affected noun that follows.
Listen to paired active/passive sentences and decide which information the speaker foregrounds.
Explain a school process using at least three present passives, then answer who performs one step using an active sentence.
Repair passive sentences with active vowels, wrong gender prefix and accusative former objects.
Write a 120–140-word news report, process description or school notice. Include at least five passive verbs and explain one event with an active sentence where the agent matters.
[callout] Model: أُعْلِنَتِ النَّتَائِجُ صَبَاحَ الْيَوْمِ، وَنُشِرَتْ عَلَى مَوْقِعِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. تُسْتَعْمَلُ هَذِهِ الطَّرِيقَةُ لِكَيْ يَطَّلِعَ جَمِيعُ الطُّلَّابِ عَلَيْهَا.
[callout] Success checklist: Use two past passives, three present passives, one feminine subject, one non-human plural and correct نائب الفاعل endings where shown.
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Draw arrows showing object → نائب الفاعل for each transformed sentence. Write the omitted agent only when it is logically recoverable.
Recognise and form past and present passives.
- form the core past passive pattern فُعِلَ;
- form the core present passive pattern يُفْعَلُ;
- identify and agree with نائب الفاعل;
- choose passive or active according to information focus.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
